title: Policy description has no minimum length for active/published policies — `Yup.string().max(1000)` only; blank description accepted on activation; violates Clause 7.5.2(a)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `description: Yup.string().max(1000)` only — no `.min()`. Blank descriptions accepted on activation.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change to: `description: Yup.string().when('status', { is: (s) => ['active','under_review'].includes(s), then: (s) => s.min(20, 'Active policies require a description of at least 20 characters'), otherwise: (s) => s.optional() }).max(1000)`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyEdit.jsx:336-343` (comment cites PM-014) implements exactly this: `description: Yup.string().when('status', { is: (s) => ['active','under_review'].includes(s), then: (s) => s.min(20, ...), otherwise: (s) => s.optional() }).max(1000)`. `PolicyCreate.jsx` is now a thin wrapper around `PolicyEdit.jsx`, which is the live create/edit form.

title: No client-side file type validation in `PolicyAIReader` before upload — no `accept` attribute on drag-and-drop; non-document files submitted; backend rejects after upload completes
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIReader.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Drag-and-drop area has no `accept` attribute and no MIME type check before `setFile`. Non-document files are submitted; backend rejects only after upload completes.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `accept=".pdf,.docx,.doc,.txt"` to the file input. In `handleDrop`/`handleFileSelect`: `const ALLOWED = ['application/pdf','application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document','application/msword','text/plain']; if (!ALLOWED.includes(file.type)) { setError('Unsupported file type. Upload PDF, DOCX, DOC, or TXT.'); return; }`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyAIReader.jsx:518` (comment cites PM-015) implements a client-side file type guard before upload begins, matching the backend's actual accepted set (PDF/DOCX/PPTX/TXT/MD — see `policy-reader.routes.js`'s multer `fileFilter`).

title: AI Reader analysis results have no path to policy register — no 'Create Draft' or 'Map to Existing Policy' action; analysis is ephemeral, not linked to policy lifecycle
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIReader.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Analysis results displayed as JSON preview only. No 'Create Draft Policy' or 'Map to Existing Policy' action button. Analysis is ephemeral and not linked to any policy lifecycle.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
After results display, add: `<Button onClick={() => router.push({ pathname: '/policy-management/create', query: { fromAnalysis: analysisId } })}><PlusCircle className="w-4 h-4 mr-2" />Create Draft from Analysis</Button>`. In `PolicyCreate.jsx`, if `fromAnalysis` query param present, pre-fill fields from analysis result via `GET /api/policy-reader/:id/results`.
fixEvidence: Implemented with a richer flow than originally requested: `PolicyAIReader.jsx` (~lines 1682-1723) now has an 'Adopt Policy & Triage Gaps' action (`handleAdoptPolicy`) that — per its own inline description — 'creates one draft policy, saves its control and requirement mappings, and sends identified gaps to Risk Triage' in one step, plus a 'Retry Risk Triage Delivery' recovery action if the risk dispatch partially fails. This links AI Reader analysis directly into the policy register (as a draft) and the framework-mapping/risk pipeline, superseding the simpler 'Create Draft' link originally proposed.

title: `avgComplianceScore` methodology opaque — no tooltip, formula, or methodology disclosure; auditor cannot determine which frameworks contribute or verify the score; violates ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyDashboard.jsx`, `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `avgComplianceScore` displayed with no tooltip, formula disclosure, or methodology description. Auditors cannot determine which frameworks contribute or verify the score.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Wrap score display in `<Tooltip content="Percentage of active framework controls covered by at least one active policy. Calculated from PolicyControlMapping records."><InfoIcon className="w-4 h-4 inline ml-1 text-muted-foreground" /></Tooltip>`.
fixEvidence: `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx:233-237` renders the 'Overall Compliance' stat with a `Tooltip` whose label reads verbatim: 'Percentage of active framework controls covered by at least one active policy. Calculated from PolicyControlMapping records.' — matching the requested fix exactly, plus a 'Recalculate' button (line 210-219) that re-runs the live calculation.

title: Compliance score not recalculated automatically after policy changes — manual 'Recalculate' button only; score stale immediately after any lifecycle event; violates Clause 9.1
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `useEffect(() => { fetchCompliance(); }, [])` — empty dependency array. Score is fetched once on mount and not refreshed after any lifecycle event.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change to `useEffect(() => { fetchCompliance(); }, [lastPolicyUpdate])` where `lastPolicyUpdate` is a context value updated whenever a policy status changes. Or add a `refetchInterval: 30000` if using React Query.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: Re-verified against the current `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx` (now a fully built dashboard, not a stub — see PM-031). The underlying score is no longer cached/fabricated (see PM-025, now computed live from `PolicyControlMapping` on every call), which reduces the practical impact, but the dashboard component itself still does not refetch on any policy lifecycle event. | Not fixed. `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx:87-119`: `fetchComplianceScore` is wrapped in `useCallback` with deps `[user, projectId, selectedTimeRange, selectedFramework]`, and the driving `useEffect` (lines 115-119) depends on exactly those same values — none of which change when a policy is approved/archived/etc. in another tab or view during the same session. There is still only a manual 'Recalculate' button (line 121, `recalculateScore`) and no automatic refetch tied to a policy-lifecycle event/context value.

title: Version history shows version numbers only — no field-level change descriptions; `changeHistory` maps as "Saved as V${version}" with no "Title changed from X to Y"; violates Clause 7.5.2(b)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/services/policy-version.service.js`
**Root Cause:** `compareVersions` returns `{changes: []}` empty array. `changeHistory` maps only as `"Saved as V${version}"` with no field-level diff.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `policy-version.service.js` `createVersion`: use `deep-diff` npm package to compute field-level changes between current and previous version. Store as `changes: diff.map(d => ({field: d.path.join('.'), from: d.lhs, to: d.rhs}))`. Render in version history timeline.
fixEvidence: Field-level change tracking is now built in end-to-end (all pieces explicitly cite PM-019): `policy.model.js:188` stores field-level change metadata on each version; `PolicyEdit.jsx:173-187,700,838` computes `changedFields`/`contentWordDiff` via `computeChangedFields`/`computeContentWordDiff` (tracks title/description/content/category/priority/tags) and submits it alongside every update; `PolicyDetailView.jsx:195` builds human-readable field-level change descriptions from that metadata for the version-history timeline.

title: Bulk delete allows deletion of active policies without elevated confirmation — generic AlertDialog for any status mix; active policy linked to Annex A controls can be deleted in same step as drafts; no impact analysis shown; violates Clause 7.5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyList.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** Generic `AlertDialog` for any status mix. Backend `bulkDelete` does not check for `active` policies or linked controls.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `PolicyList.jsx` bulk delete handler: `const activeCount = selectedPolicies.filter(p => p.status === 'active').length; if (activeCount > 0) { setConfirmText(\`\${activeCount} active policies will be permanently deleted. Type DELETE to confirm:\`); setRequireTextConfirm(true); }`. Backend: `const activeLinked = await PolicyControlMapping.countDocuments({policyId: {$in: ids}}); if (activeLinked > 0) return res.status(400).json({error: \`\${activeLinked} control mappings will become orphaned. Remove mappings first.\`});`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: Backend bulk logic is now in `policy.repository.js`'s `bulkOperation()` (called from `policy.controller.js`'s `bulk` handler), not inline in the controller as originally cited. | Not fixed. `policy.repository.js:750-756`: the `action === 'delete'` branch is a plain `Policy.updateMany({policyId: {$in: policyIds}, isDeleted: false, ...scopeFilter}, {$set: {isDeleted: true, ...}})` with no filtering on `status` and no check against `PolicyControlMapping` linkage — every selected policy is soft-deleted regardless of status (unlike the sibling `archive`/`activate` actions in the same function, which DO enforce `allowedSourceStatuses`). No elevated/typed confirmation UI specific to active-policy bulk delete was found in `PolicyList.jsx`.

title: Status field allows any `policy.write` user to set `active`/`closed`/`expired` — all lifecycle states shown in dropdown without checking `policy.approve` permission; write-only users can bypass review; violates Annex A 5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/routes/policy.routes.js`
**Root Cause:** All 9 lifecycle statuses shown in the status dropdown without checking `policy.approve` permission. `PUT /:id` route guards `policy.write` only.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Frontend: `const allowedStatuses = hasPermission('policy.approve') ? ALL_STATUSES : ['draft','under_review','archived']; return allowedStatuses.map(s => <SelectItem key={s} value={s}>{s}</SelectItem>)`. Backend `updatePolicy`: `if (['active','closed','expired'].includes(body.status) && !hasPermission(req.user, 'policy.approve')) return res.status(403).json({error: 'Insufficient permissions to set this status'});`.
fixEvidence: Fixed via the same PM-001 workflow overhaul, at both layers: `PolicyEdit.jsx:205,1267` (comments cite PM-022) restricts the status dropdown options by permission. More importantly, the status field is now categorically excluded from `PUT /policies/:policyId` server-side — `policy.validation.js:59-62` rejects any `status` in the update body outright, and `policy-version.service.js:47-60` strips it as defence in depth — so lifecycle changes can ONLY happen via `POST /policies/:policyId/transition`, which is gated by `requirePermission('policy.approve')` at the route level (`policy.routes.js:136-141`). A `policy.write`/`policy.update`-only user has no code path to reach `active`/`closed`/`expired` at all, not just a hidden-but-bypassable dropdown.

title: Single `policy.read` PermissionGate covers entire feature — `policy.approve`/`policy.archive`/`policy.delete` not enforced at action level; write+read user can trigger archive and bulk-delete without approve permission; violates Annex A 5.3
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/app/policy-management/page.jsx`, `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/routes/policy.routes.js`
**Root Cause:** `page.jsx` has one `<PermissionGate permission="policy.read">` wrapper. Approve/archive/delete actions only guarded by `policy.write`. No `policy.approve` or `policy.delete` route guards in backend.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add per-action gates: `<PermissionGate permission="policy.approve"><ApproveButton /></PermissionGate>`. `<PermissionGate permission="policy.delete"><BulkDeleteButton /></PermissionGate>`. Backend: `router.delete('/bulk', requirePermission('policy.delete'), bulkDeleteController)`. `router.post('/:id/approve', requirePermission('policy.approve'), approveController)`.
fixEvidence: The security-relevant half of this defect (no backend route guards) is fixed: `policy.routes.js` now enforces per-action permissions route-by-route — `POST /:policyId/transition` requires `policy.approve` (line 136-141, this is the approve/reject/reassign path), `DELETE /:policyId/permanent` (hard delete) requires `policy.admin` (line 332-336), `POST /:policyId/restore` requires `policy.admin` (line 161-165), `DELETE /:policyId` (soft delete) requires `policy.delete` (line 353-357), and plain read/update actions remain on `policy.read`/`policy.update`. This is the definitive security boundary and is enforced server-side regardless of what the frontend shows. Frontend: `page.jsx:258-260` still wraps the whole page in one `policy.read` gate (expected — that's page-level access, not action-level), and `PolicyList.jsx` uses `PermissionHide` around several `policy.update`-gated bulk actions (lines 1176-1594); the review approve/reject actions are instead gated by the backend-computed `metadata.isReviewer` flag in `ReviewDetail.jsx`, an arguably more precise per-review mechanism than a blanket permission string.

title: Duplicate `useEffect` for change tracking in `PolicyEdit.jsx` lines 467–474 and 643–650 — both compare `JSON.stringify(formik.values)`; both fire per value change causing double re-renders
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyEdit.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Identical `useEffect` comparing `JSON.stringify(formik.values)` appears at both lines 467–474 and 643–650. Both fire per value change causing double re-renders and double dirty-state updates.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Delete the duplicate `useEffect` block at lines 643–650. Keep only the instance at lines 467–474. Run `npm test -- --testPathPattern=PolicyEdit` to verify no regressions.
fixEvidence: Only one occurrence of `JSON.stringify(formik.values)` remains in `PolicyEdit.jsx` (line 652, inside a single change-tracking effect) — the duplicate block has been removed.

title: AI generation polling timeout hardcoded at 5 minutes — no option to continue waiting or retry; comprehensive policy generations may legitimately exceed this limit
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIGenerator.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `setTimeout(() => { clearInterval(interval); setError('Generation timed out'); }, 300000)` — 5 minutes hardcoded with no user-configurable option.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Make configurable: `const POLL_TIMEOUT = process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_AI_POLL_TIMEOUT_MS || 300000`. Add "Still waiting…" message after 2 minutes with a "Keep waiting" button that resets the timeout counter. On timeout, offer "Retry" rather than just displaying an error.
fixEvidence: `PolicyAIGenerator.jsx:463-500` now scales the timeout to the requested length (`GENERATION_TIMEOUTS = {brief: 2min, standard: 5min, comprehensive: 10min}`) instead of a flat 5 minutes, and on timeout offers `handleContinuePolling` (lines 502-579) — a 'Continue Waiting' action that resumes polling for another 10 minutes rather than just showing a dead-end error.

title: `PolicyComplianceDashboard` references unimplemented stub sub-components — `FrameworkCoverageHeatmap`, `ComplianceTrendChart`, `ComplianceGapsPanel`, `PolicyComplianceDetailModal`, `ComplianceExportButton` missing or stubs; dashboard renders incomplete
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx` **Root Cause:** `FrameworkCoverageHeatmap`, `ComplianceTrendChart`, `ComplianceGapsPanel`, `PolicyComplianceDetailModal`, `ComplianceExportButton` all imported but commented out or absent from filesystem. **Claude Fix Prompt:** Short-term: replace each stub import with an inline `

Coming soon

` placeholder component. Track each component as a separate backlog item so the dashboard renders without errors.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The 5 sub-components now live at `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/compliance/*.js` (plain `.js`, not `.jsx`), imported by `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx:60-64`. | All 5 components exist as real, substantial implementations, not stubs: `FrameworkCoverageHeatmap.js` (414 lines), `ComplianceTrendChart.js` (429 lines), `ComplianceGapsPanel.js` (429 lines), `PolicyComplianceDetailModal.js` (539 lines), `ComplianceExportButton.js` (214 lines) — all wired into `PolicyComplianceDashboard.jsx` (lines 341,357,381,389,220) and rendering real data, not placeholder 'Coming soon' cards.

title: `FrameworkMapping` is read-only — no CRUD capability from UI; all mappings must be created during policy creation or via AI analysis; no manual control-to-policy mapping
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/FrameworkMapping.jsx`
**Root Cause:** Component fetches and displays mappings only. No CRUD operations. All mappings must be created during policy creation or via AI analysis.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add `<Button size="sm" onClick={() => setAddMappingOpen(true)}><Plus className="w-4 h-4 mr-1" />Add Control Mapping</Button>`. Create `AddControlMappingDialog` with framework selector, control selector (from `GET /api/frameworks/:id/controls`), and `POST /api/policies/:id/control-mappings` submission.
fixEvidence: Not fixed. `FrameworkMapping.jsx` still has no live 'Add Control Mapping' action anywhere. An 'Actions' table column with `Edit`/`Delete` `IconButton`s calling `handleEdit(record)`/`handleDelete(record)` does exist in the source (lines ~307-332) but the entire block is inside a `/* ... */` comment and `handleEdit`/`handleDelete` are never defined anywhere in the file — this is dead, non-functional code, not a working CRUD capability. The component (confirmed by grepping for POST/mutation calls) remains fetch-and-display-only; mappings are still only created during policy creation, via AI analysis, or via the separate `PolicyEdit.jsx` control-mappings editor.

title: No template preview before generation — must save to see output; no custom template creation UI in `TemplateMarketplace`
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/TemplateMarketplace.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `handleGenerate` immediately saves without a preview step. Users cannot review generated content before it enters the policy library.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Split into two steps: (1) `POST /api/templates/:id/preview` with form parameters returns rendered HTML — display in a `<Dialog>` with the generated content. (2) Add "Confirm & Save" button in the dialog that calls the existing save endpoint.
fixEvidence: Not fixed. `TemplateMarketplace.jsx:249-286`'s `handleGeneratePolicy` still calls `POST /templates/:id/generate` with `preview: false` hardcoded, then immediately calls `POST /policies` to create the policy in the same action — there is no intermediate preview dialog showing the rendered content before it is saved. The 'Template Detail Modal' (lines 632-751) only shows template metadata (description, frameworks, variables, stats), never the actual variable-interpolated content. Notably, the backend's `generate` endpoint already accepts a `preview` flag (unused by the frontend), suggesting a preview capability exists server-side but was never wired into the UI.

title: Public template routes have no rate limiting — `GET /popular`, `GET /`, `POST /validate`, `POST /parse` vulnerable to DoS; OWASP A04:2021
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/routes/policy-template.routes.js`
**Root Cause:** `GET /popular`, `GET /`, `POST /validate`, `POST /parse` registered before `authenticate` middleware. No rate limiter applied to public routes.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add before public routes: `const publicLimiter = rateLimit({windowMs: 15*60*1000, max: 30, message: 'Too many requests, please try again later', standardHeaders: true, legacyHeaders: false}); router.use(['/popular', '/validate', '/parse'], publicLimiter);`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: A standalone `policy-template.routes.js` no longer exists — template routes are now registered inside `policy.routes.js` itself. | The underlying vulnerability (unauthenticated public access) no longer exists — the architecture changed. `policy.routes.js:38-45`: `router.use(authenticate);` is now called BEFORE the template routes are registered (`/templates`, `/templates/validate`, `/templates/:id`, `/templates/:id/generate`), and each carries an explicit `requirePermission('policy.read'|'policy.create')` guard. There is no longer an unauthenticated 'public' surface on these endpoints to DoS anonymously; abuse would require a valid authenticated session, which is a materially different (and much lower) risk than the originally-reported unauthenticated public routes. No dedicated per-route rate limiter was added on top of authentication, but that is a lesser residual concern than the defect as originally scoped.

title: Field name inconsistencies between models and export controllers — `frameworks[].name` vs `.framework` in CSV export line 3069; owner null-safety missing; `reviewers[].userId` vs `.reviewerId` mismatch line 5107; CSV exports contain `undefined` values
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/controllers/policy.controller.js`
**Root Cause:** `exportPolicies` at line ~3069: uses `f.framework` (field doesn't exist on model — should be `f.name`). `reviewer.reviewerId` at line ~5107 (should be `reviewer.userId`). CSV exports contain `undefined` values for these columns.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Line ~3069: change `f.framework` to `f.name`. Line ~5107: change `reviewer.reviewerId` to `reviewer.userId`. Add integration test: generate export CSV, parse it with `csv-parse`, assert no `undefined` or `"undefined"` string in any field.
fixEvidence: `policy.controller.js:312-458`'s `exportPolicies` (`GET /policies/export`) now explicitly documents and applies both fixes (comments literally cite PM-036 four times): frameworks are resolved via `ComplianceFramework` and mapped using `f.name` (line 374-376), and reviewers are resolved via `WorkflowEntry`'s `metadata.assignedTo` and exposed as `reviewer.userId` (line 390-401), further resolved to a human-readable display name before CSV output (PM-L03 follow-up hardening) rather than a raw ObjectId.

title: Framework list not refreshed when user switches projects in `PolicyCreate` — fetched on mount only; stale frameworks remain; users may select frameworks from wrong project
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyCreate.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `useEffect(() => { fetchFrameworks(); }, [])` — missing `currentProject?.id` in dependency array. Stale frameworks from the previous project remain in the dropdown after project switch.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Change to `useEffect(() => { if (currentProject?.id) fetchFrameworks(currentProject.id); }, [currentProject?.id])`. Update `fetchFrameworks` to accept `projectId` and pass it as a query param: `GET /api/frameworks?projectId=${projectId}`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: `PolicyCreate.jsx` is now a thin wrapper delegating to `PolicyEdit.jsx`, which owns the live framework-fetch logic. | `PolicyEdit.jsx:250-289`: `useEffect(() => { const fetchFrameworks = async () => { ... }; fetchFrameworks(); }, [selectedProject])` — the effect's dependency array now includes `selectedProject` (sourced from Redux via `useSelector(selectSelectedProject)`), so the framework list is refetched via `cfrsService.getAuthorityFrameworks(projId)` every time the active project changes.

title: Potential memory leak in `PolicyAIReader` polling intervals — `setInterval` not guaranteed to clear on component unmount; orphaned intervals continue executing API calls after navigation
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIReader.jsx`
**Root Cause:** `const intervalRef = useRef(null)` then `intervalRef.current = setInterval(...)` — but the cleanup `return () => clearInterval(intervalRef.current)` races with the assignment when the component unmounts before the first interval tick.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Restructure: `useEffect(() => { let id; if (isPolling) { id = setInterval(pollStatus, 3000); } return () => clearInterval(id); }, [isPolling])`. The `id` is always defined in the closure at the point the cleanup function is created, eliminating the race.
fixEvidence: Re-architected around `setTimeout`-chained recursive polling guarded by both an `isMountedRef` and an `activePollJobIdRef` (explicitly documented at `PolicyAIReader.jsx:393`: 'Uses isMountedRef + pollTimeoutRef to prevent memory leaks on unmount'). Every poll step checks `!isMountedRef.current || activePollJobIdRef.current !== jobId` before scheduling the next `setTimeout` (lines 406,413,463 etc.) and clears `pollTimeoutRef.current` on completion/failure/supersession, eliminating the original race between assignment and cleanup.

title: No client-side file size validation in `PolicyAIReader` — 50MB limit enforced only by backend Multer; users discover rejection only after upload completes; no size indication in upload UI
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-client-panel/src/components/policy-management/PolicyAIReader.jsx` **Root Cause:** File size enforced only by Multer (50MB). No client check before `setFile`. Users discover rejection only after upload completes. **Claude Fix Prompt:** In `handleFileSelect`/`handleDrop`: `const MAX_SIZE = 50 * 1024 * 1024; if (file.size > MAX_SIZE) { setError(\`File too large (\${(file.size/1024/1024).toFixed(1)}MB). Maximum size is 50MB.\`); return; }`. Display remaining capacity: `

Max file size: 50MB

`.
fixEvidence: CITATION UPDATE: The backend limit is now 20MB (`policy-reader.routes.js:58`: `limits: { fileSize: 20 * 1024 * 1024 }`), not the originally-reported 50MB — the frontend fix correctly matches the current 20MB backend limit. | `PolicyAIReader.jsx:508-512`: `const MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES = 20 * 1024 * 1024; ... if (file.size > MAX_FILE_SIZE_BYTES) { setError(\`File too large (...). Maximum size is 20MB.\`); ... }`, with the 20MB limit also displayed in the upload UI (line 917).

title: Policy-to-UCL control mapping sync is fire-and-forget with no retry and (for the requirement-mappings path) no logging — a failed `onPolicyMappingCreated`/`onPolicyMappingRemoved` call silently desyncs the org-wide UCL verdict ledger from `PolicyControlMapping`, with zero alerting
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 6.1.3 (SoA data integrity) / ISO/IEC 27007:2019 §6.3.2 (verifiable evidence)
description:
**Files:** `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/policy.controller.js` — the `setRequirementMappings` handler's `setImmediate(...)` block (lines 1058-1090) and the `setUclMappings` handler's `setImmediate(...)` block (lines 1108-1128)
**Root Cause:** Both handlers respond to the client (`res.json(...)`) BEFORE running the UCL sync, inside a fire-and-forget `setImmediate(async () => { ... })`. In the `setRequirementMappings` path, every `complianceSync.onPolicyMappingCreated(...)`/`onPolicyMappingRemoved(...)` call (lines 1072, 1080-1082, 1087) is chained with a bare `.catch(() => {})` — a failure is silently discarded with no `logger.warn`/`logger.error` call at all, and the enclosing `try { ... } catch { /* non-critical */ }` (line 1089) would swallow it a second time even if it weren't already caught. The sibling `setUclMappings` path is slightly better — its single `complianceSync.onPolicyUclMappingChanged(...)` call (line 1119) does have a `.catch(err => logger.warn(...))` — but neither path has any retry, dead-letter queue, or reconciliation job to actually repair the drift once logged.
**Impact:** Whenever the UCL sync call transiently fails (DB blip, downstream validation error, timeout) — which is entirely plausible since this runs post-response with no user-visible feedback — the org-wide UCL verdict ledger (`ucl-control.model.js` / `client-compliance` layer, the same system GRC_Framework_QA_Agent's coverage view and this module's own FrameworkMapping UI both read from) silently diverges from the policy's own `PolicyControlMapping`/requirement-mapping state. The policy-management UI will show a mapping as present/removed while the cross-module UCL coverage report (and anything downstream of it, e.g. audit SoA views) does not reflect it — a genuine SoA data-integrity gap with no operator-visible signal for the `setRequirementMappings` path, and only a log line (no alert/retry) for `setUclMappings`. This is the same defect class Vendor_Management_QA_Agent already flagged for its own vendor→UCL sync (VM-026, 'confirmed-lossy fire-and-forget event').
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
```
1. In policy.controller.js's setRequirementMappings sync block (~line 1058-1090), replace every
   bare `.catch(() => {})` on complianceSync.onPolicyMappingCreated/onPolicyMappingRemoved with
   `.catch(err => logger.warn('[complianceSync] policy requirement-mapping sync failed', { error: err.message, policyId: req.params.policyId, requirementId: rid }))`
   at minimum, matching the logging already present in setUclMappings.

2. Add a durable retry mechanism (BullMQ job with backoff, or a periodic reconciliation pass
   comparing PolicyControlMapping/requirement-mapping state against the UCL ledger for the
   affected policyId) rather than relying on best-effort in-process fire-and-forget calls for
   data that feeds compliance/SoA reporting.
```

title: FrameworkMapping.jsx's coverage-gap drill-down always renders the literal placeholder 'Multiple controls' - PM-011 is not actually fixed
description:
policy.repository.js::coverageGaps (lines 695-702) builds each gap entry with missingControls:[] hardcoded to an empty array, never populated from the actual uncovered-control set. FrameworkMapping.jsx:493-496 renders {gap.missingControls?.join(', ') || 'Multiple controls'} - since the array is always empty, [].join(', ') returns '' (falsy), so this line ALWAYS falls through to the literal string 'Multiple controls', for every domain, every framework, every time.

Auditor-facing breakage: the QA tracker marked PM-011 'fixed' because a drawer UI and a 'View Details' button now exist, but the actual per-gap content behind 'Missing: ...' was never wired to real data - every single gap entry reads 'Missing: Multiple controls' verbatim. An auditor trying to sample the Statement-of-Applicability-shaped gap gets a UI that visually implies drill-down capability but delivers zero additional information beyond the aggregate percentage already shown on the stats card.

title: Policy lifecycle transitions never trigger a UCL recompute; coverage status can be stale relative to real-world policy state
description:
workflowTransition.service.js has zero references to complianceSync/recomputeControlCoverage anywhere in the file. policy.controller.js calls complianceSync.* only from setRequirementMappings and setUclMappings - never from the transition handler (the only path that changes policy.status).

Auditor-facing breakage: when a policy that already carries mappings (attached while draft) is finally approved (under_review -> active), nothing re-triggers recomputeControlCoverage for its mapped controls - the UCL ClientControl.coverageScore stays stale at its prior (likely gap) value until an unrelated event happens to touch the same control. The same is true in reverse when a policy is archived/retired: the UCL score doesn't drop until something else coincidentally recomputes it. For an auditor sampling evidence on a specific date, /grc-framework's coverage view can lag the real, current state of the policy register with no visible 'last recalculated' indicator tying the two together.

title: `PolicyDetailView.jsx` has zero permission gating on any action button — Archive/Restore/Edit/Export/Share/Clone all render unconditionally regardless of `policy.approve`/`policy.admin`/`policy.update`
description:
**Checklist row:** §1.2 — RBAC permission gates on every UI action: every create/update/delete/approve button in the frontend is wrapped in `PermissionGate`/`usePermission`, not just the page-level read gate.
**Files:** `PolicyDetailView.jsx` — repo-wide grep for `PermissionGate`/`PermissionHide`/`usePermission` inside this file returns zero matches. The Archive button (line ~1321, opens the confirm modal at line ~2364, calls `handleArchive` at line 611 which POSTs `/:policyId/transition` with `targetState:'archived'`), the Restore button (line ~2416, calls `handleRestore`), the Edit button (lines 1255/1619/1845), Export menu (1272-1281), Share (1290), and Clone (1305) are all rendered to any user who can reach the detail page (i.e. anyone holding `policy.read`, including via a project grant) with no permission-based hide/disable of any kind.
**Root Cause:** PM-023's prior fix (see that record's `fixEvidence`) verified the *backend* route guards (`policy.approve` on `/transition`, `policy.admin` on `/restore`, `policy.delete` on soft-delete) and verified `PolicyList.jsx`'s bulk-action `PermissionHide` wrapping and `ReviewDetail.jsx`'s `isReviewer`-flag gating — but never checked `PolicyDetailView.jsx` itself, which has a materially different (and effectively ungated) action surface from either of those two files.
**Impact:** Not an authorization bypass — the backend still rejects an unauthorized Archive/Restore call server-side (per PM-023) — but any `policy.read`-only viewer (e.g. a project member with a read-only Custom Project Role, or an external auditor account scoped to read access) sees fully clickable Archive/Restore/Edit controls that will fail with a raw error toast on click, a confusing and inconsistent UX that also makes it impossible to tell from the UI alone who is actually authorized to perform these actions on a given policy.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `PolicyDetailView.jsx`, import `PermissionHide` (same component already used in `PolicyList.jsx`) and wrap: the Archive `MenuItem`/button in `<PermissionHide permission="policy.approve" allowProjectGrant projectId={policy.projectId}>` (Archive goes through `/transition`, gated by `policy.approve` server-side), the Restore button in `<PermissionHide permission="policy.admin">` (no project-grant equivalent — `policy.admin` is a SUPERADMIN-only org-wide permission per `augmentPermissionsWithProjectGrant.js`'s `PROJECT_ADMIN_MODULE_PERMISSIONS`, which does not include `admin`), and the Edit button/menu item in `<PermissionHide permission="policy.update" allowProjectGrant projectId={policy.projectId}>` (matching the pattern already at `PolicyList.jsx:1587,1621`).

title: Policy workflow transitions have no optimistic-lock/precondition guard — `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` does an unconditional `updateOne` with no `status: currentState` filter, so concurrent transitions can silently last-write-wins
requirement: ISO 27001:2022 Clause 8.1 operational planning and control
description:
**Checklist row:** §6.4 — Race conditions on concurrent transitions handled: two actors transitioning the same record concurrently don't produce a corrupted or double-applied state (optimistic locking / version check / atomic update).
**Files:** `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` (`workflowTransition.service.js:50-86`) reads `currentState` via a separate, non-atomic lookup (`_getEntityCurrentStatus` / latest `WorkflowEntry`) well before the eventual write, validates `targetState` is in `def.transitions[currentState]`, then later (line 167) calls `_updateEntityStatus()`, which (lines 418-463) executes `Model.updateOne({ _id: entityId }, { $set: { status: modelValue } })` — no `status: currentState` (or any version field) is included in the query filter, so the write is unconditional.
**Root Cause:** No optimistic-concurrency mechanism (a `status`-matching filter, a `__v` version check, or a Mongo transaction) exists anywhere in this read-check-write sequence for `policy` (or any other entity type driven by this same shared service).
**Impact:** Two concurrent `POST /:policyId/transition` calls against the same policy while it is `under_review` (e.g. two reviewers/admins independently reading the same starting state) can both pass the allowed-transition check against the same stale `currentState`, both `WorkflowEntry.create()` a transition record, and both call `_updateEntityStatus` — the later write silently wins with no conflict signal to either caller, no rejection, and no reconciliation. The result: a `WorkflowEntry` audit-trail entry exists recording a transition (e.g. to `rejected`) that was never actually reflected in the policy's real `status` field because a later concurrent call (e.g. to `active`) overwrote it — a workflow-integrity/traceability gap where the audit log and the entity's real state can silently diverge.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `WorkflowTransitionService._updateEntityStatus` (`workflowTransition.service.js:418-463`), add the precondition to the filter and check the result: `const result = await Model.updateOne({ _id: entityId, [field]: currentState }, { $set: { [field]: modelValue } }); if (result.matchedCount === 0) { const err = new Error('Policy state changed concurrently — please refresh and retry'); err.statusCode = 409; throw err; }`. This requires threading `currentState` into `_updateEntityStatus`'s call at line 167 (it's already in scope in `transition()`). Apply the same fix to the `evidence`/`vendor`/etc. call sites since this is a shared service — out of scope for this policy-management-focused run, but worth flagging to those modules' owners.

title: No rate limiting on authenticated AI-generation-trigger endpoints — `POST /policy-ai/generate`, `/bulk-generate`, and `/generations/:id/refine` have zero request-rate middleware
description:
**Checklist row:** §13.3 — Rate limiting on public/expensive endpoints: public template endpoints, AI-generation triggers, share-link access are rate-limited.
**Files:** `policy-ai.routes.js` — repo-wide grep for `rateLimit`/`Limiter`/`slowDown` inside `vibrantix-backend/src/modules/policy/` returns no middleware usage anywhere. `POST /generate` (line 76-83), `POST /bulk-generate` (line 88-94), and `POST /generations/:id/refine` (line 146-153) carry `authenticate`, `tierContext`, `accessGuard`, `requirePermission('policy.create'|'policy.update')`, and `requireProjectMembership` — but no per-route or per-user rate limiter.
**Root Cause:** This is a distinct gap from PM-034 (already fixed — that defect was specifically about the *unauthenticated* public template routes, `GET /templates*`, which are now behind `authenticate` and no longer need a rate limiter per that record's own `fixEvidence`, which explicitly notes 'No dedicated per-route rate limiter was added on top of authentication' as a residual, lower-priority concern). The AI generation endpoints are a different, higher-cost surface: each call triggers a real external HTTP round-trip to the `ai_policy_generator_python` microservice and reserves AI credits via `policy-ai-metering.service.js`.
**Impact:** An authenticated user (or a compromised/scripted session) can burst-call `/generate`/`/bulk-generate`/`/refine` far faster than a human would, which (a) creates unnecessary load against the external AI microservice with no platform-side throttle, and (b) — per the already-open PM-058 (credit reservation not released on client-abandoned polling) — widens the window in which concurrent/rapid generation requests could reserve credits that are never cleanly reconciled. Distinct from PM-058 itself: that defect is about reservation/release bookkeeping after a request is accepted; this one is about nothing bounding how many such requests can be fired in the first place.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
Add an `express-rate-limit` (or the platform's existing rate-limit middleware factory, if one exists — check `vibrantix-backend/src/middleware/` for a reusable limiter used elsewhere, e.g. evidence upload) instance keyed by `req.userId` + `req.orgId`, e.g. `const aiGenerationLimiter = createRateLimiter({ windowMs: 60_000, max: 5 })`, and apply it to `router.post('/generate', aiGenerationLimiter, ...)`, `router.post('/bulk-generate', aiGenerationLimiter, ...)`, and `router.post('/generations/:id/refine', aiGenerationLimiter, ...)` in `policy-ai.routes.js`.

title: Policy workflow notifications cover assignment only — approval/rejection/needs-revision decisions and any other status change never notify the policy owner, even though the shared dispatch pipeline is real and already wired for the assignment case
description:
**Checklist row:** §5.1 — Key lifecycle events dispatch a notification: assignment, due-date approaching/overdue, approval requested, approval decision, status change — each fires through the standard dispatch pipeline, not an ad hoc or silent path.
**Files:** `WorkflowTransitionService.transition()` (`workflowTransition.service.js:226-271`) does contain a real, working notification dispatch via `notificationService.dispatch()` (correctly module/label/deep-link-mapped for `entityType: 'policy'` per `_entityTypeToModule`/`_entityTypeLabel`/`_buildNavigateTo`) — but the dispatch is gated behind a single condition: `if (['assigned', 're-assign'].includes(targetState) && opts.assignedTo)` (line 227). Every other transition a policy can make — `under_review → active` (approved), `under_review → rejected`, `under_review → needs_revision`, `active → archived`/`expired → archived` — falls through this same function with no notification call at all; the `if` block is skipped entirely and nothing else in `transition()` dispatches one.
**Root Cause:** Only the assignment event was ever wired to the notification pipeline; the approval-decision and status-change events the checklist separately calls out were never added, even though the same function already has everything it needs (actor, entity, previous/new state) to dispatch them.
**Impact:** A policy author/owner who submits for review is notified when a reviewer is assigned, but never learns — except by manually reopening the policy — that their policy was approved, rejected, or sent back for revision. For a document-control workflow where the whole point is timely review completion (ISO 27001 Clause 7.5.2), the one event that actually matters to the author (the decision) is silent.
**Claude Fix Prompt:**
In `workflowTransition.service.js`, after the existing assignment-notification block (after line 271, still inside `transition()`), add a second dispatch for decision/status-change transitions, e.g.: `if (['active', 'rejected', 'needs_revision', 'archived', 'expired'].includes(targetState)) { const notificationService = require('../notification/notification.service'); const ownerId = await this._getEntityOwnerId(entityType, entityId); if (ownerId) { notificationService.dispatch({ targetUserId: ownerId, organizationId: opts.organizationId?.toString(), notificationType: 'review_decision', sourceModule: _entityTypeToModule(entityType), entityId: entityId?.toString(), entityType, message: `Your ${_entityTypeLabel(entityType)} was ${targetState}`, actorId: userId?.toString(), navigateTo: _buildNavigateTo(entityType, entityId, opts), priority: 'medium' }).catch(err => logger.error({ err }, '[WorkflowTransition] decision notification dispatch failed')); } }` — add a small `_getEntityOwnerId(entityType, entityId)` helper that reads `createdBy`/`owner` off the right model per `entityType` (reusing the existing `MODEL_MAP` from `_updateEntityStatus`).
